statement.summary: Proposition 10.1 is frozen as nine Props whose conjunction is `rateLawStatement`: the two inequalities of the first display (`rateLowerStatement` in ℕ, `rateUpperStatement` in ℝ), the decay-rate sandwich (`rateGapStatement`), the vanishing of the gap bound and the limit c(n,d) → 1 − 1/p_1 (`Filter.Tendsto` along d : ℕ → ∞ for fixed n, σ), and four readings of the universality-class sentence (common limit for equal p_1; even n → 1/2; prime p → 1 − 1/p; 1/2 extremal; liminf ≥ 1/2).
deltas: Alphabet Σ is `Fin σ`; |S_{n^d}| = `numSS n d σ`, P^unif = `probUnif n d σ` (ℝ).
p_1(n) = `Nat.minFac n`; N/p_1 = `n ^ d / minFac n` is ℕ-division, exact since p_1 ∣ n^d for d ≥ 1 (`p1_dvd_pow`).
log_b x = `Real.logb b x`; all log arguments are > 0 and bases are 2 or σ ≥ 2 under the hypotheses, so mathlib's log conventions never fire.
n^{d−1} uses ℕ-subtraction `d - 1`, exact since 1 ≤ d (the limit statements quantify d only inside `Tendsto`, where small d is irrelevant).
Limits 'as d → ∞' are `Filter.Tendsto (fun d : ℕ => …) atTop (𝓝 L)` with n and σ fixed outside (pointwise in n, σ; the paper claims nothing uniform).
c(n,d) carries σ explicitly: `decayRate n d σ`.
The universality-class sentence is split into four Props (common limit for equal p_1, even class, prime class, extremal 1/2) plus the floor parenthetical as liminf ≥ 1/2 in ε–D form.

maps.label: Proposition 10.1 = conjunction of nine Props

tex.text: Let $p_1=p_1(n)$ be the smallest prime factor of $n$

lean.text:
rateBoundsStatement ∧ rateGapStatement ∧ rateGapBoundTendstoStatement ∧
    rateLimitStatement ∧ rateUniversalityStatement ∧ rateEvenClassStatement ∧
    ratePrimeClassStatement ∧ rateExtremalClassStatement ∧ rateFloorStatement

maps.note: The proposition is split into its sentences: two-sided bound, sandwich, vanishing gap bound, limit, and four readings of the universality-class sentence plus the 'floor' parenthetical. The auxiliary proof-chain Prop `rateProofPrefactorStatement` is NOT part of it.

maps.label: p_1(n) = smallest prime factor

tex.text: $p_1=p_1(n)$ be the smallest prime factor of $n$

maps.note: mathlib `Nat.minFac n` is the least prime factor for n ≠ 1; every statement assumes 2 ≤ n, so it is prime.

maps.label: N = n^d

lean.text: n ^ d / p1 n

maps.note: N is never a separate name in Lean; it is written out as `n ^ d` (ℕ) or `(n : ℝ) ^ d` (ℝ).

maps.label: for all n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1, σ ≥ 2
maps.note: Same quantifiers in `rateLowerStatement`, `rateUpperStatement`, `rateGapStatement`. The limit statements drop `1 ≤ d` (only large d matter) and quantify `∀ n σ` before the limit in d.

maps.label: σ^{N/p_1} ≤ |S| ≤ 2 log₂(n) n^{d−1} σ^{N/p_1}

lean.text: rateLowerStatement ∧ rateUpperStatement

maps.note: The displayed chain is split into its two inequalities.

maps.label: lower bound σ^{N/p_1} ≤ |S_{n^d}|

lean.text: σ ^ (n ^ d / p1 n) ≤ numSS n d σ

maps.note: Stated in ℕ (both sides are natural numbers).

maps.label: |S_{n^d}|

lean.text: numSS n d σ
Nat.card {s : Config n d (Fin σ) // IsShiftSymmetric s}
∃ v : Lat n d, v ≠ 0 ∧ shift v s = s

maps.note: `numSS n d σ` = cardinality of the configurations over `Fin σ` fixed by some nonzero translation (Definition 2.3).

maps.label: exponent N/p_1 (ℕ-division)

lean.text: n ^ d / p1 n

maps.note: ℕ-division; exact because p_1 ∣ n ∣ n^d for d ≥ 1 (proved representation check `p1_dvd_pow`; the proof casts it to the real quotient via `cast_E`).

maps.label: upper bound |S| ≤ 2 log₂(n) n^{d−1} σ^{N/p_1}

lean.text:
(numSS n d σ : ℝ) ≤
      2 * Real.logb 2 (n : ℝ) * (n : ℝ) ^ (d - 1) * (σ : ℝ) ^ (n ^ d / p1 n)

maps.note: Stated in ℝ (2 log₂ n is irrational in general); |S| cast to ℝ.

maps.label: prefactor 2 log₂(n) n^{d−1}

lean.text: 2 * Real.logb 2 (n : ℝ) * (n : ℝ) ^ (d - 1)

maps.note: log₂ = `Real.logb 2` (argument n ≥ 2 > 0); n^{d−1} uses ℕ-subtraction `d - 1`, exact since 1 ≤ d.

maps.label: σ^{N/p_1} on the right

lean.text: (σ : ℝ) ^ (n ^ d / p1 n)

maps.note: Real base, natural exponent `n ^ d / p1 n` (exact ℕ-division).

maps.label: c(n,d) := −log_σ P^unif_{n^d} / N

lean.text: -Real.logb (σ : ℝ) (probUnif n d σ) / (n : ℝ) ^ d

maps.note: The paper suppresses σ; Lean has `decayRate n d σ`. P^unif > 0 under the hypotheses, so `Real.logb`'s conventions at 0 never fire.

maps.label: P^unif_{n^d} = |S|/σ^{n^d}

lean.text: (numSS n d σ : ℝ) / (σ : ℝ) ^ (n ^ d)

maps.note: Shared definition from Corollary 7.1, real division.

maps.label: 0 ≤ (1 − 1/p_1) − c(n,d) ≤ log_σ(2n^{d−1}log₂n)/N

lean.text:
0 ≤ (1 - 1 / (p1 n : ℝ)) - decayRate n d σ ∧
      (1 - 1 / (p1 n : ℝ)) - decayRate n d σ ≤
        Real.logb (σ : ℝ) (2 * (n : ℝ) ^ (d - 1) * Real.logb 2 (n : ℝ)) / (n : ℝ) ^ d

maps.note: Chain split into a conjunction of two inequalities, same quantifiers n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1, σ ≥ 2.

maps.label: (1 − 1/p_1) − c(n,d)

lean.text: (1 - 1 / (p1 n : ℝ)) - decayRate n d σ

maps.note: 1/p_1 is real division (p_1 ≥ 2).

maps.label: log_σ(2 n^{d−1} log₂ n)/N

lean.text: Real.logb (σ : ℝ) (2 * (n : ℝ) ^ (d - 1) * Real.logb 2 (n : ℝ)) / (n : ℝ) ^ d

maps.note: Argument ≥ 2 > 0 (log₂ n ≥ 1), base σ ≥ 2; N = (n:ℝ)^d > 0. Factor order as in the paper.

maps.label: gap bound → 0 as d → ∞

lean.text:
∀ n σ : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → 2 ≤ σ →
    Tendsto
      (fun d : ℕ =>
        Real.logb (σ : ℝ) (2 * (n : ℝ) ^ (d - 1) * Real.logb 2 (n : ℝ)) / (n : ℝ) ^ d)
      atTop (𝓝 0)

maps.note: `Filter.Tendsto` along d : ℕ → ∞ (atTop) for each FIXED n ≥ 2, σ ≥ 2 (quantifiers outside the limit; no uniformity in n or σ is claimed, nor by the paper). Values at d = 0 (where d − 1 truncates) do not affect the limit.

maps.label: c(n,d) → 1 − 1/p_1(n)

lean.text:
∀ n σ : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → 2 ≤ σ →
    Tendsto (fun d : ℕ => decayRate n d σ) atTop (𝓝 (1 - 1 / (p1 n : ℝ)))

maps.note: Limit in d (the variable of the preceding arrow), for fixed n ≥ 2 and σ ≥ 2; `Tendsto … atTop (𝓝 L)`.

maps.label: universality classes determined solely by p_1

tex.text:
Asymptotically in $d$, lattice sides fall into
\emph{universality classes} determined solely by their smallest prime
factor

lean.text:
∀ n m σ : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → 2 ≤ m → 2 ≤ σ → p1 n = p1 m →
    ∃ L : ℝ, Tendsto (fun d : ℕ => decayRate n d σ) atTop (𝓝 L) ∧
      Tendsto (fun d : ℕ => decayRate m d σ) atTop (𝓝 L)

maps.note: Formalized as: equal p_1 ⇒ a common limit exists. Only this direction ('determined solely by') is frozen; that different p_1 give different classes follows from `rateLimitStatement` and is not a separate Prop.

maps.label: even n on the class c = 1/2

tex.text: with even $n$ on the extremal class $c=1/2$

lean.text:
∀ n σ : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → Even n → 2 ≤ σ →
    Tendsto (fun d : ℕ => decayRate n d σ) atTop (𝓝 (1 / 2))

maps.note: 'On the class' = the limit is 1/2 (c(n,d) < 1/2 occurs at finite d, e.g. c(2,2) = 1/4 at σ = 2, so only the limit reading is true).

maps.label: 1/2 is the extremal class value
maps.note: 'Extremal' = least among all class values 1 − 1/p_1(n), attained exactly at even n (pure real arithmetic in minFac).

maps.label: the floor permitted by Theorem 6.3

lean.text: ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ D : ℕ, ∀ d : ℕ, D ≤ d → 1 / 2 - ε ≤ decayRate n d σ

maps.note: Read as liminf_{d→∞} c(n,d) ≥ 1/2, in ε–D form, for fixed n ≥ 2, σ ≥ 2. A finite-d floor would be false (c(2,2) = 1/4). The attribution 'permitted by Theorem 6.3' is not formalized: the Lean proof derives the floor from the limit and `rateExtremalClassStatement`, not from Theorem 6.3.

maps.label: primes p on c = 1 − 1/p

lean.text:
∀ p σ : ℕ, p.Prime → 2 ≤ σ →
    Tendsto (fun d : ℕ => decayRate p d σ) atTop (𝓝 (1 - 1 / (p : ℝ)))

maps.note: Limit as d → ∞ for each prime p and fixed σ ≥ 2.
